results.title: Correlations Between Subjective and Objective Caregiver Burden Change Over Time - Oncology Nurse Advisor
results.content:
Title: Correlations Between Subjective and Objective Caregiver Burden Change Over Time - Oncology Nurse Advisor
# Correlations Between Subjective and Objective Caregiver Burden Change Over Time. A recent analysis of caregiver burden sheds light on the relationships between subjective and objective measures of caregiver burden. “The number of caregiver tasks rather than task intensity was associated with increased objective and subjective burden,” the study investigators wrote in their report. The study was a case series of patient-caregiver dyads in which the patients had terminal cancer. The study investigators evaluated demographics, measures of subjective caregiver burden (using the Zarit Burden Inventory), patient symptom burden, a variety of objective measures of caregiver burden, and details on high-intensity tasks and time spent caregiving in assessments of correlations between subjective and objective burden. Overall, relationships between subjective burden and a variety of measures evaluated in the study tended to be significant, with correlations and levels of significance varying over time. When associations were evaluated on a within-person or between-person basis, subjective burden tended to demonstrate positive associations with most of the measures of objective burden both within and between caregivers. However, the time spent on high-intensity tasks was significantly associated with subjective burden only at the within-person level (*P* <.01). Additional analyses indicated a tendency for increased objective burden for caregivers throughout time for all but IADL tasks, while on average, subjective burden appeared to demonstrate little change with time. Subjective burdens were also positively associated with the spouse caregiver role, while being a Black caregiver showed a negative association with subjective burden. In addition to finding that the number of caregiver tasks may influence caregiver burden more greatly than task intensity does, the investigators also concluded that the time spent on tasks tended to increase, with objective burden increasing over time while subjective burden did not. Results differed by caregiver group, but caregivers reporting greater average subjective burden typically also reported greater objective burden. results.title: The unseen burden of family caregiving and how AI can help - McKnights Home Care
results.content: AI-driven applications can help schedule rides, send reminders and provide contextual information to older adults and their caregivers. These AI companions can offer empathetic interaction, assist with daily tasks, and provide emotional support while reducing the dependency on human caregivers. AI systems can also provide reminders for medical appointments and follow-up care, ensuring that older adults adhere to their treatment plans and caregivers stay informed about their health status. By providing a sense of companionship and emotional support, AI can help older adults maintain a higher quality of life while giving caregivers a much-needed emotional respite. AI provides consistent support and interaction, particularly when human caregivers are unavailable, to ensure that older adults never feel alone. By providing continuous monitoring, enhancing the quality of interactions, coordinating essential services, and offering emotional support, AI can transform the caregiving experience. As we move forward, embracing AI-driven solutions will be crucial in ensuring that older adults receive the care they need while supporting the well-being of their dedicated caregivers.

Conclusion: Non-attendance for clinical psychology appointments was associated with (a) young age, (b) prolonged waiting time (over six months), (c) complex psychological problems, and (d) new patients. results.title: The Emotional Impact of Caregiving on Families—and How In-Home Help Can Relieve the Burden | TLC Caregivers
results.content: At **TLC Caregivers**, we understand that caregiving isn’t just about managing tasks — it’s about managing emotions, relationships, and self-care, too. In this blog, we’ll explore the emotional impact caregiving can have on families and how in-home care can provide relief, ensuring everyone’s well-being is prioritized. While the act of caregiving stems from love and duty, it often leads to emotional stress for the family members involved. Caregiver burnout occurs when a family caregiver feels physically and emotionally exhausted, often due to the overwhelming responsibilities of caregiving. Caregiving can sometimes lead to strained relationships, both with the person being cared for and with other family members. While caregiving may be an emotional journey, **TLC Caregivers** is here to support families in every way possible.
